text:
maria_cs: Heads up — Neuroforge (Dedicated trial) usage fell to ~12% of baseline yesterday. Renewal ~6 weeks out. Looks like a hard drop across endpoints. Can someone triage? :warning:

sam_se: On it. Quick Q: is this a traffic routing/latency issue or auth failures? Any 5xx spikes?

data_analyst_amy: Pulled metrics: overall tokens down 88% day-over-day. Top 3 endpoints affected: /v1/complete, /v1/embed, /v1/chat. No notable 5xx spike in logs, but 401s ticked up slightly around 02:10 UTC. Chart: https://dash.redwood.internal/nb/neuroforge/usage (internal)

jordan_ae: New purchasing lead (Claire Park) started 10 days ago per convo with AM. They also opened a short competitive pilot with LexaAI last week — we saw a small surge to Lexa during that window. Claire said cost was a big question.

leo_onboard: From onboarding side: their eval cluster finished last Friday; we saw a few long tails on session warmup that could affect perceived perf. I can re-run warmup script.

maria_cs: Thanks. Amy — can you paste the SQL you ran? Share counts so we can pin time windows.

data_analyst_amy: Sure — ran this quick slice:

```
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hr, count(*) AS calls
FROM usage.events
WHERE customer = 'neuroforge'
  AND ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC
LIMIT 72;
```

Drop started ~2025-11-02 02:00 UTC. Baseline avg ~4.2k calls/hr; yesterday peaked at ~500 calls/hr.

ops_bot: [ALERT] customer-neuroforge: sudden-traffic-drop detected. Runbook: triage-route-traffic -> assigned to oncall-eng. Incident ID: INC-20251102-42

sam_se: I'll run a quick synthetic against their dedicated endpoint and share latency+auth headers. If auth failing we'll get a 401 combo.

sam_se: (after tests) Synthetic shows 200 for health-check but auth header ttl mismatch on a small percentage of requests -> 401s with token "expired_token" in logs. Token issuance appears to have rotated incorrectly last night for that trial cluster.

jordan_ae: Claire flagged cost -> they throttled internal jobs and paused heavy batch embedding runs. That could explain some drop but not to 12%. Looks like both cost-led throttling + token rotation bug.

maria_cs: Plan proposal:
- Sam: hotfix token rotation for trial cluster and coordinate with infra (ETA 2h). Owner: @sam_se.
- Leo: run warmup and restart the onboarding batch jobs with a small pilot (ETA 6h). Owner: @leo_onboard.
- Amy: prepare a one-pager with hourly call counts + affected endpoints for the exec sync (ETA 3h). Owner: @data_analyst_amy.
- Jordan: ask Claire for competitive pilot details and confirm if they'd like Redwood to run a cost/latency comparison demo (ETA today EOD). Owner: @jordan_ae.

leo_onboard: Will also add a quick checklist for customer to re-enable paused jobs (small step-by-step).

jordan_ae: For renewal convo — recommend offering a short cost-safety pack: 2-week discounted burst + a dedicated cost report. If they accept, we can propose a follow-up QBR in 2 weeks.

maria_cs: Good. If token fix + warmup doesn't recover to >70% baseline in 24h escalate to SE-High.

data_analyst_amy: Uploaded CSVs to the folder shared with AE: /shared/neuroforge/usage-dumps/2025-11-02.csv

sam_se: Hotfix deployed to trial cluster. Rotated tokens and patched TTL logic. Monitoring shows 401s dropping to baseline.

ops_bot: [RECOVERY] customer-neuroforge: traffic normalized to 84% of baseline 45 minutes after patch. Incident INC-20251102-42 resolved (auto).

maria_cs: Great — Jordan, start the cost-safety pack outreach. Leo, confirm warmup run completed. Amy, get the final hour-by-hour slide for the exec sync. We'll reconvene in 2h for status unless any regressions. :eyes:
